title: Inverse image commutes with internal extension along arbitrary ring objects
statement:
Let $g\colon Z\to X$ be any morphism of schemes. Let $R,S$ be commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ with the sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and let $\varphi\colon R\to S$ be a morphism of ring objects. Write $F=g^{-1}$ for inverse image of abelian sheaves [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], with its strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]; it is symmetric monoidal [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], so $F(R)$ and $F(S)$ are commutative ring objects of $\Sh(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ and $F(\varphi)$ is a morphism of ring objects. Write $F_R=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ on $R$-module objects and $F_S=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ on $S$-module objects [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. There is a natural isomorphism of functors $\Mod_R\to\Mod_{F(S)}$
\[
F_S\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\ \cong\ \operatorname{Ext}_{F(\varphi)}\circ F_R,
\qquad
F_S(S\otimes_R M)\cong F(S)\otimes_{F(R)}F_R(M),
\]
where relative tensor and extension of scalars are those of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The coefficient rings on the right are the actual inverse images $F(R),F(S)$; no identification with a ring pulled back from a point is assumed.

proof.text: Write $F=g^{-1}$ and $G=g_*$. The strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and monoidal adjunction [lem-sfb-finite-monoidal-adjunction] on [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] give the lifted adjunctions $F_A\dashv H_A$ for $A=R,S$, by [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction], where $H_A=\operatorname{mapMod}(G)\,;\operatorname{Res}_{u_A}$ and $u_A:A\to GF(A)$ is the adjunction unit. Compose with the extension--restriction adjunctions of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Thus $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\,;F_S$ is left adjoint to $H_S\,;\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$, and $F_R\,;\operatorname{Ext}_{F\varphi}$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_{F\varphi}\,;H_R$. The image ring $F(R)$ is commutative by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], so its extension--restriction adjunction applies.

source.place: Final clause: restricting the extended presentation to a stratum and then to a pro-étale cover; inverse image of the balancing coequalizer

proof.text: Naturality of the adjunction unit gives $\varphi\,;u_S=u_R\,;G(F\varphi)$ as morphisms into the twice-transported monoid $GF(S)$. By the composition and congruence isomorphisms for restriction in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], restriction first along $u_S$ and then along $\varphi$ is naturally isomorphic to restriction first along $G(F\varphi)$ and then along $u_R$. In Lean use Mod.comapComp, Mod.comapCongr and this unit-naturality equality, explicitly typed using unitAlgHom to keep the transported monoid structures.

source.place: Section Adjoint functors, definition-adjoint: the adjunction unit is natural; restriction acts by precomposing the scalar action

proof.text: Transport of modules [def-sfb-modobj-transport] commutes with restriction: G.mapModComapIso applied to $F\varphi$ identifies $\operatorname{Res}_{F\varphi}\,;\operatorname{mapMod}(G)$ with $\operatorname{mapMod}(G)\,;\operatorname{Res}_{G(F\varphi)}$. Combine its inverse with step 2, whiskering by the remaining restriction and inserting functor associators. This constructs an isomorphism $e:H_S\,;\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{F\varphi}\,;H_R$ between the two right adjoints.

source.place: Final clause: restricting the extended presentation to a stratum and then to a pro-étale cover; inverse image of the balancing coequalizer

proof.text: Transport the second composite adjunction across $e^{-1}$ (Adjunction.ofNatIsoRight). Its right adjoint is now exactly the right adjoint of the first composite adjunction. Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq gives the required natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\,;F_S\cong F_R\,;\operatorname{Ext}_{F\varphi}$, as an isomorphism of module-valued functors. Therefore linearity, invertibility and naturality are already part of the constructed isomorphism; no separate underlying-object comparison is needed. The coefficient rings are the actual $F(R),F(S)$ throughout.
